result.answer: Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of the same problem. It usually has two parts: a base case, which stops the calls, and a recursive case, which reduces the problem toward that base case. Example: factorial(n) = n × factorial(n-1), with factorial(1) = 1.
